facts: The appellants are the sons and daughters of the accused N. Ramakrishnaiah in C.C. No.64 of 1992 on the file of the Principal Special Judge, for SPE & ACB Cases, Hyderabad.
He was charged for the offence u/s. 5 (1)(e) read with S. 5 (2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 possessing the pecuniary resources disproportionate to the known sources of income.
The accused worked as Executive Engineer as on the date of search of his house and other properties.

Evidence was adduced and the Special Judge found the accused guilty, convicted him for the above mentioned offence and sentenced him to undergo simple imprisonment for one year and to pay a fine of Rs.20, 000/- in default to suffer simple imprisonment for three months.
The Special Judge also directed that item No 1 to 4 of the assets shall be sold in public auction and the sale proceeds shall be confiscated to the State.
As noted above, during the pendency of the appeal before the High Court, the appellant died, therefore, the sentence of imprisonment stood abated against the appellant.
issues: Whether S. 482 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 permits the course to be adopted
Whether the High Court can review its own judgment by exercising inherent powers
petitioner_arguments: Since the appellants are willing to deposit money there is no reason as to why the High Court should not permit release of the properties in favour of the legal heir of deceased accused.
According to the appellants in an appropriate case the fine amount as imposed can be enhanced and the custodial sentence can be reduced.
respondent_arguments: Since Criminal Appeal was dismissed there was no scope for passing the order as the Court had become functus officio
The High Court did not find any substance in the plea and it was held that S. 482 Cr.P.C. did not empower the Court to review its own judgment by exercising inherent powers
court_reasoning: We need not go into that question because S. 16 of the Act reads as follows:
The High Court has rightly noted that it is the present value of the properties which is of relevance and not the value of the assets at the relevant point of time of seizure.
holding: It is open to the appellants to participate in the auction for sale of the properties in question as and when held.
